2607.11649.title: Closing the Loop: An Access-Control Architecture for Automated, Anomaly-Driven Network Revocation in IoT Deployments
2607.11649.paper_summary: Network-based anomaly detection for IoT devices has matured to the point of reporting strong detection accuracy, yet most published systems stop at raising an alert and leave the question of automated enforcement to future work or to a programmable data plane that few real networks operate. This paper presents an access-control architecture that closes that loop using only standard, already-deployed protocols. Devices authenticate via IEEE 802.1X with EAP-TLS, and a RADIUS server acts as a continuous policy decision point capable of evicting an active session via a Change-of-Authorization Disconnect-Request and permanently excluding a device through certificate revocation. A central, contextual access policy engine continuously consumes the anomaly detector's output and actuates this response over a narrowly restricted channel to the RADIUS server; the same engine is designed to be extensible to other access types, though this paper evaluates only the network access-control mechanism. This mechanism is driven by an anomaly signal from a one-class detector adapted from a prior MUD/SDN-based design, replacing its per-flow multi-model pipeline with passive traffic capture and a single fused model that combines a cluster-based, a volumetric, and a protocol-signature score. On a single testbed device, the detector reaches an AUC of 0.9964 and detects all 24 evaluated attack scenarios (eight attack types at three intensities) using roughly 43$\times$ less training data than the reference design, and the resulting alerts reliably trigger the automated disconnect-then-revoke response, which we measure to evict a device from the network in 335.8\,ms on average and complete certificate revocation in a further 111.5\,ms. We report this evaluation as a demonstration of the closed-loop architecture rather than of the detector itself, and discuss multi-device generalization as a concrete next step.
2607.11649.paper_summary_zh: 物聯網設備的基於網絡的異常檢測已經成熟到能夠報告強大的檢測準確率，但大多數已發表的系統僅停留在發出警報，並將自動執行的問題留給未來的工作或少數實際運行的可編程數據平面。本文提出了一種訪問控制架構，利用僅有的標準、已部署的協議來閉合這一循環。設備通過IEEE 802.1X與EAP-TLS進行身份驗證，RADIUS伺服器作為一個持續的政策決策點，能夠通過授權變更斷開請求驅逐活動會話，並通過證書撤銷永久排除設備。一個中央的上下文訪問政策引擎不斷消耗異常檢測器的輸出，並通過一個狹窄限制的通道對RADIUS伺服器進行此響應；同一引擎設計為可擴展到其他訪問類型，儘管本文僅評估網絡訪問控制機制。該機制由來自先前MUD/SDN基礎設計的一類檢測器的異常信號驅動，將其每流的多模型管道替換為被動流量捕獲和一個融合模型，該模型結合了基於聚類的、基於體積的以及基於協議簽名的分數。在單一測試設備上，檢測器達到0.9964的AUC，並檢測到所有24個評估的攻擊場景（八種攻擊類型在三種強度下），使用的訓練數據大約比參考設計少43$\times$，而所產生的警報可靠地觸發自動斷開然後撤銷的響應，我們測量到平均335.8毫秒內將設備驅逐出網絡，並在進一步的111.5毫秒內完成證書撤銷。我們將這一評估報告作為閉環架構的示範，而非檢測器本身，並討論多設備泛化作為具體的下一步。
